Adversarial comparison against the blueprint at C:/Users/ChaseStanley/Downloads/files/brand_assets/blessed-dressed/public/images/ai/collar-point-95-btn.png.

Tried to reject the photo on the following grounds and could not:
- Sibling substitution: ruled out. Tips are sharp (not Curve Point 7.5), leaves are emphatically long (not Point 7.0 or Fashion Point 5.8), the throat button is EXPOSED (not Point 7.0 Hidden Button), there is no tab (not Regular 8.5 with Tab), and there are no buttons at the point tips (not a button-down). The option is unambiguously identifiable within one second.
- Button count: exactly one visible button in both images. No extra or missing buttons.
- Placket: both the drawing and the photo show a concealed/fly front with only the throat button exposed and no topstitched placket edges. No second button appears in either crop.
- Point length: leaf-drop-to-collar-span ratio is 0.78 in the photo vs 0.73 in the drawing on rough pixel measurement, reading as the same emphatic long point and clearly longer than the 7.0/8.5 cm siblings.
- Button placement: ~62% down the leaf vs ~65% in the drawing.
- Edge stitching: present, parallel to the edge, carried around both points, at a comparable offset.
- Orientation: detail view of the front face in both. No front/back confusion.
- Background: seamless neutral grey, no location, architecture, furniture, scenery or props.
- Annotation: no numbers, units, dimension or leader lines, arrows, callouts, coloured guide marks, ruler ticks, labels or watermark anywhere in frame.

The four surviving discrepancies are all Minor and all trace to the locked prompt's 'worn on a male model' instruction (the blueprint is shot on an empty form) or to natural drape. None alters the construction a customer would be choosing between.

Framing footnote: the collar's bounding box occupies ~36% of the frame, marginally under the 40-80% dominance target, but the blueprint's own collar bounding box occupies the same ~36% — the photo matches the drawing's framing rather than deviating from it, and the collar is plainly the dominant subject.
